design_detail: Meta-analysis of (C)BT and pharmacotherapy studies for generalized anxiety disorder, with comparison of efficacy across modalities
comparison_group: Control conditions; pharmacotherapy (direct and indirect comparisons)
population: Adults with generalized anxiety disorder
sample_size_detail: 65 (C)BT and pharmacological studies included; total pooled participants not reported in abstract
rationale: PubMed type Meta-Analysis; abstract describes meta-analytic techniques across 65 studies. Designs of included studies (e.g., RCTs) not explicitly stated in abstract.

design_detail: Canadian Task Force on Preventive Health Care recommendation statement on depression screening in adults (CMAJ)
population: Adults (general and selected populations) considered for depression screening
sample_size_detail: Guideline; no sample size
rationale: Title 'Recommendations on screening for depression in adults' and PubMed type Practice Guideline. No abstract in file.

design_detail: RANZCOG best practice statement (C-Obs 48) on perinatal mental health care
population: Pregnant and postpartum women in Australia/New Zealand
sample_size_detail: Professional college statement; no sample size
rationale: Citation describes a college 'Best practice statement', i.e., a consensus/practice statement. Citation-only file.

design_detail: Journal article (J Reprod Infant Psychol 2012) on patient-, provider-, and system-level barriers and facilitators to addressing perinatal depression; design not determinable from citation
population: Perinatal depression care (patients, providers, systems); specific sample not available
sample_size_detail: Not available (citation only; not indexed in PubMed)
rationale: Coded from ACOG citation alone (article not in PubMed; earlier file had a wrong abstract, disregarded). Title suggests a barriers/facilitators study (possibly qualitative, survey, or review), but design and N cannot be determined, so coded Other.

design_detail: Online ACOG/UMass Chan webinar/training course on addressing perinatal mental health conditions in obstetric settings
population: Obstetric clinicians (training audience)
sample_size_detail: Training resource; no sample size
rationale: Citation is a pathlms.com ACOG webinar course URL, i.e., a training program resource rather than a study.

design_detail: Cross-sectional mailed/distributed survey of ACOG Fellows on prenatal depression screening and antidepressant prescribing
population: US obstetrician-gynecologists (ACOG Fellows) providing prenatal care
sample_size_detail: 1000 Fellows sampled; 379 responded (37.9%); 288 provided prenatal care and answered the depression screening/prescribing questions
rationale: Clinician survey describing practices and opinions; associations examined descriptively without a comparative effect estimate of treatment.

design_detail: Retrospective/secondary analysis of a prospective cohort at one US academic center; pre- vs post-implementation epochs of perinatal collaborative care, propensity-score covariate adjustment, race-by-epoch interaction
severity_measure: Propensity score: maternal age, insurance, parity, tobacco, substance use history, chronic medical problem or mental health history (presence only); GDM and preterm birth for postpartum models. No symptom score or severity proxy.
comparison_group: Pre-implementation epoch (no concurrent untreated control); White individuals as referent for race comparisons
population: Black or White pregnant and postpartum people receiving prenatal care at Northwestern Medicine-affiliated offices, Chicago, deliveries 2015–2019
sample_size_detail: Pre-implementation 2286 (262 Black, 2024 White); post-implementation 2424 (313 Black, 2111 White); treatment-recommendation analyses limited to positive screens (PHQ-9 >9)
rationale: Pre/post comparison without a concurrent unexposed control, so not quasi-experimental per protocol; PS adjustment includes only presence of mental health history. Restriction to PHQ-9 >9 for secondary outcome is restriction on screen-positive status, not severity adjustment.

design_detail: Descriptive program evaluation of MCPAP for Moms (statewide perinatal psychiatry access program): development, implementation, utilization and cost over first 18 months
population: Massachusetts perinatal women and their obstetric/other providers served by MCPAP for Moms
sample_size_detail: 1123 women served; 87 Ob/Gyn practices enrolled; 100 trainings conducted
rationale: Reports program utilization counts and cost per woman without a comparison group or effect estimate.

design_detail: Cross-sectional analysis of nationally representative US survey data 2005–2009; chi-square and adjusted prevalence ratios comparing pregnant vs nonpregnant women with past-year MDE
severity_measure: Adjusted prevalence ratios reported but covariates not listed in abstract
comparison_group: Nonpregnant women of reproductive age with past-year MDE
population: US women aged 18–44 with past-year major depressive episode, 2005–2009
sample_size_detail: 375 pregnant and 8657 nonpregnant women with past-year MDE
rationale: Non-randomized comparison by pregnancy status with adjusted prevalence ratios (aPR); covariate set unavailable, so severity adjustment Unclear and coded as excl. severity by default.

design_detail: Systematic review and network meta-analysis of double-blind RCTs of 21 antidepressants for acute MDD (PROSPERO CRD42012002291)
population: Adults with major depressive disorder
sample_size_detail: 522 trials comprising 116477 participants
rationale: Explicit systematic review and NMA restricted to double-blind randomised controlled trials; quasi-randomised trials excluded.

design_detail: Systematic review, random-effects meta-analysis and network meta-analysis of SSRI/SNRI exposure in pregnancy and PPHN
comparison_group: Unexposed pregnancies; between-SSRI comparisons in NMA
population: Pregnant women and their offspring (SSRI/SNRI exposure)
sample_size_detail: 11 studies; 156978 exposed women and offspring reported; total pooled (exposed plus unexposed) not reported
rationale: Included retrospective cohort and case-control studies only; abstract reports exposed count but not total pooled participants.

design_detail: Systematic review and meta-analysis (AHRQ-type comparative effectiveness review) of antidepressant treatment outcomes in pregnancy and postpartum
comparison_group: Other antidepressants, placebo/no treatment, nondrug treatments
population: Pregnant or postpartum women with depression and their children
sample_size_detail: 6 RCTs and 15 observational studies; total pooled participants not reported in abstract
rationale: PubMed type Systematic Review; abstract states 6 randomized controlled trials and 15 observational studies provided evidence.

design_detail: Single-center, 6-week, double-blind, placebo-controlled RCT of sertraline with 1-week single-blind placebo lead-in
population: Women with major depression onset within 3 months postpartum, single US center
sample_size_detail: 38 entered placebo lead-in (abstract n=38); 2 removed for lead-in response; 36 randomized (17 sertraline, 19 placebo) = ITT; 33 evaluable; 29 completed week 7; DSM-IV 4-week-onset subset n=27
rationale: Randomized double-blind placebo-controlled trial; full text gives 36 randomized after lead-in.

design_detail: Systematic review and network meta-analysis of randomised trials of pharmacological treatments for GAD (PROSPERO CRD42018087106)
population: Adult outpatients with generalised anxiety disorder
sample_size_detail: 89 trials, 25441 patients randomly assigned to 22 active drugs or placebo
rationale: Abstract states systematic review and NMA of randomised trials, 89 trials with 25441 patients.

design_detail: Clinical narrative review of treatment of peripartum bipolar disorder (Obstet Gynecol Clin North Am)
population: Pregnant and postpartum women with bipolar disorder
sample_size_detail: Narrative review; no sample size
rationale: Full text is a clinical overview without search methods or study selection; PubMed type Review.

design_detail: Danish national register linkage (Medical Birth Register and Psychiatric Central Register, 1973–1993); relative risk of psychosis admission within 91 days postpartum vs non-puerperal women
severity_measure: No adjustment described in abstract; relative risks of admission rates (first vs readmissions reported separately)
comparison_group: Non-puerperal women in the general Danish female population
population: Danish women giving birth 1973–1993 and the general Danish female population
sample_size_detail: 1253 psychosis admissions within 91 days after delivery; denominator births/person-time not reported in abstract
rationale: Registry comparison of admission rates (RR) with no covariate adjustment reported in abstract. N is the count of postpartum admissions, not the full cohort.

design_detail: Review of 8 published cohort studies to generate hypotheses, then population-based case-malformed-control study in EUROCAT Antiepileptic Study Database (19 European registries, 1995–2005); logistic regression adjusted for maternal age, birth year, registry
severity_measure: Adjusted only for maternal age, year of birth, and reporting registry; authors note no other confounder data available
comparison_group: Malformed controls (non-chromosomal and chromosomal); exposure contrasts: carbamazepine vs no AED, valproic acid, other AED monotherapy
population: Registered births/fetuses with major congenital malformations in 19 European registries covering 3.88 million births, 1995–2005
sample_size_detail: 11790 cases (5 malformation subgroups), 69883 non-chromosomal controls, 11763 chromosomal controls; 131 carbamazepine-monotherapy-exposed registrations; literature review component: 8 cohort studies, 2680 exposed pregnancies
rationale: Hypothesis-testing primary analysis is the adjusted case-control study (the review only generated indications), so coded observational rather than SR. Covariates limited to maternal age, birth year, registry; no epilepsy severity.

design_detail: Multicenter prospective observational PK study with frequent sampling before and early in pregnancy; population mixed-effects modeling of lamotrigine clearance vs gestational week and estradiol
population: Pregnant women with epilepsy on lamotrigine without interacting medications
sample_size_detail: 25 pregnancies in 22 participants
rationale: Drug clearance study (LTG-CL/F) without a confounder-adjusted clinical outcome comparison.

design_detail: Prospective PK study of lamotrigine concentrations from preconception and monthly through pregnancy and postpartum
population: Women on lamotrigine monotherapy before and during pregnancy
sample_size_detail: 14 women on LTG monotherapy
rationale: Measures lamotrigine clearance changes across pregnancy; no clinical outcome comparison.

design_detail: PK study comparing lamotrigine apparent clearance at preconception, each trimester, and postpartum (ANOVA, paired t-tests)
population: Pregnant women treated with lamotrigine (epilepsy) with steady-state data before, during, and after pregnancy
sample_size_detail: 12 pregnancies with complete steady-state data
rationale: Apparent clearance and dose requirements across pregnancy; pharmacokinetic design.

design_detail: Prospective observational study of placental passage (umbilical cord:maternal plasma ratio) of atypical antipsychotics and haloperidol at delivery, with descriptive obstetric outcomes
comparison_group: None (between-drug comparison of placental passage ratios)
population: Pregnant women with laboratory-confirmed antipsychotic use proximate to delivery
sample_size_detail: 54 women included; 50 complete maternal-infant sample pairs
rationale: Primary aim quantifies placental passage (drug concentrations); obstetric outcomes only described, no adjusted comparison.

design_detail: Multicenter 8-week double-blind placebo-controlled RCT of quetiapine 600 or 300 mg/day (BOLDER I)
population: Adult outpatients with bipolar I or II disorder in a major depressive episode
sample_size_detail: 542 randomized (360 bipolar I, 182 bipolar II); number analyzed not given in abstract
rationale: Patients randomly assigned to quetiapine or placebo; PubMed type RCT.

design_detail: Multicenter 8-week double-blind placebo-controlled RCT of quetiapine 300 or 600 mg/day (BOLDER II)
population: Patients with bipolar I or II disorder in a depressive episode
sample_size_detail: 509 randomized; 59% completed; ANCOVA/LOCF primary analysis
rationale: Randomized double-blind placebo-controlled trial; 509 randomized.

design_detail: Multicenter 8-week double-blind placebo-controlled RCT of quetiapine 300/600 mg/d and lithium (EMBOLDEN I, NCT00206141)
population: Adults with bipolar I or II disorder in an acute major depressive episode
sample_size_detail: 802 randomized: quetiapine 300 mg n=265, quetiapine 600 mg n=268, lithium n=136, placebo n=133
rationale: Patients randomly allocated to four arms; PubMed type RCT.

design_detail: Systematic review of systematic reviews (umbrella review) of lurasidone for bipolar depression, AMSTAR/R-AMSTAR quality grading, narrative synthesis
comparison_group: None (synthesis of reviews; underlying RCTs vs placebo)
population: Patients with bipolar disorder treated with lurasidone
sample_size_detail: 12 systematic reviews included; no pooled participant count (no quantitative synthesis)
rationale: Included units are systematic reviews (SRs of RCTs or observational studies eligible); included reviews mainly covered the few lurasidone RCTs. Component primary-study designs not tabulated.

design_detail: Single-patient case report of serial lurasidone serum concentrations and bipolar symptoms from second trimester to 3 months postpartum
population: One primiparous woman with bipolar disorder on lurasidone
sample_size_detail: Single case
rationale: PubMed type Case Reports, but the content is serum drug-concentration monitoring and dose changes; PK precedes case report in the decision order, so coded PK.

design_detail: Prospective cohort of valproate-exposed infants of women with epilepsy compared with matched-pair controls and controls from a larger AED study; includes maternal VPA serum levels
severity_measure: Matched-pair controls used but matching variables not stated in abstract; no seizure-related adjustment reported
comparison_group: 26 matched-pair controls and 116 controls from a larger antiepileptic drug study
population: Infants of women with epilepsy receiving valproic acid (monotherapy or combination), Germany
sample_size_detail: 14 VPA-monotherapy and 12 VPA-combination exposed infants; 26 matched-pair controls; 116 additional controls
rationale: Comparison with matched controls (matching counts as adjustment), but matching factors and any other adjustment unknown from abstract; comparisons otherwise appear crude.

design_detail: Lancet letter on in-utero valproate exposure and neural tube defects; design not determinable from file
population: Pregnancies exposed to valproate (epilepsy), details not available
sample_size_detail: Not available (no abstract)
rationale: File has only metadata: PubMed types 'Comparative Study; Letter', no abstract. Likely an observational research letter, but design, adjustment, and N cannot be determined, so coded Other.

design_detail: Prospective multinational cohort (Japan, Italy, Canada) of offspring of mothers with epilepsy; malformation incidence by AED, dose, level, and polytherapy
severity_measure: Crude incidence comparisons; background factors examined as risk factors, no adjusted model described
comparison_group: Offspring without AED exposure; between-AED comparisons
population: Offspring of mothers treated for epilepsy in Japan, Italy, and Canada
sample_size_detail: 983 offspring prospectively analyzed; exposed/unexposed split not given in abstract
rationale: Abstract reports crude malformation incidences (3.1% unexposed vs 9.0% exposed) and dose-response; no covariate adjustment described.

design_detail: Letter reporting case(s) of valproic acid teratogenicity
population: Infant(s) exposed to valproic acid in utero
sample_size_detail: Number of cases not available (no abstract)
rationale: No abstract; PubMed types 'Case Reports; Letter' indicate a case report. Number of cases unknown.

design_detail: Case series describing dysmorphic features of infants exposed to valproate in pregnancy
population: Infants exposed in utero to sodium valproate/valproic acid, UK
sample_size_detail: 4 exposed infants (3 surviving)
rationale: Describes four exposed infants without a comparison group.

design_detail: Single case report of a male with fetal valproate syndrome and autism
population: One child with prenatal valproate exposure
sample_size_detail: Single patient
rationale: Reports one patient; PubMed type Case Reports.

design_detail: Cohort/comparison study of cognitive and motor function at 5.5 years in children of mothers with epilepsy vs control children (Finland), with within-group risk-factor analysis
severity_measure: Primary group comparison appears crude; within-study-group analysis examined maternal partial seizures, seizures in pregnancy, paternal education, and AED exposure, but whether these were jointly modeled is not stated
population: Children of epileptic mothers (89% AED-exposed in utero) and control children, all with normal general intelligence
sample_size_detail: 104 children of epileptic mothers, 105 control children
rationale: Abstract reports group differences without described adjustment; within-group analysis of seizure factors (epilepsy severity analogs) vs AED exposure may have been multivariable but cannot be confirmed.

design_detail: 1970 Lancet article on neonatal coagulation defect after maternal anticonvulsant treatment; design not determinable from file
population: Neonates of mothers treated with anticonvulsants in pregnancy
sample_size_detail: Not available (no abstract)
rationale: File has only title and metadata (PubMed type 'Journal Article', no abstract); could be a case series or comparative clinical study, so design is indeterminate and coded Other.

design_detail: Systematic search (PubMed, Embase 1999–2011) and random-effects meta-analysis of weight change by antipsychotic and exposure duration (MOOSE-guided)
comparison_group: Pre-post weight change within antipsychotic arms (placebo arms also extracted)
population: Adults treated with antipsychotics in clinical trials (mixed psychiatric diagnoses)
sample_size_detail: 307 articles (one paper treated as two datasets); 257 reported weight change (603 records); total pooled participants not reported
rationale: Meta-analysis of clinical trials; authors state 'only RCTs were included' (inclusion criteria also mention controlled clinical trials). No pooled N reported.

design_detail: Systematic review and meta-analysis of metabolic syndrome prevalence and relative risk across schizophrenia, bipolar disorder, and MDD, with meta-regression
comparison_group: Between-diagnosis comparisons; matched general population controls; antipsychotic-naive participants
population: People with severe mental illness (schizophrenia/psychosis, bipolar disorder, MDD)
sample_size_detail: Pooled MetS prevalence from 198 studies, n=52678
rationale: Abstract describes a systematic review and meta-analysis (N=198 studies; n=52678); designs of included studies not stated.

design_detail: Two population-based retrospective cohorts (UK THIN, Hong Kong CDARS) among prior antipsychotic users, continuers vs discontinuers, propensity-score fine-stratification weighting; plus updated meta-analysis
severity_measure: PS fine-stratification weighting for 'potential confounding factors'; covariate list not in abstract
comparison_group: Women who used antipsychotics before pregnancy but discontinued during pregnancy
population: Nondiabetic women with antipsychotic prescriptions before first pregnancy, UK and Hong Kong
sample_size_detail: 2351 in THIN and 763 in CDARS; continuer/discontinuer split not in abstract; meta-analysis component size not reported
rationale: Primary analysis is the PS-weighted cohort comparison (meta-analysis is an add-on update). Severity adjustment cannot be confirmed without covariate list.

design_detail: Systematic review and meta-analysis of GDM risk by preconception mood, anxiety, psychotic, and eating disorders
comparison_group: Women without the specified preconception mental disorder
population: Pregnant women with preconception mental disorders
sample_size_detail: 22 observational studies (mostly retrospective cohorts); pooled participants not reported in abstract
rationale: Abstract states 22 observational studies met inclusion criteria; PubMed types Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.

design_detail: Systematic review and random-effects meta-analysis of lithium safety and efficacy in pregnancy and postpartum (case-control, cohort, interventional studies)
comparison_group: Lithium-unexposed pregnancies; no lithium for relapse prevention
population: Pregnant and postpartum women with bipolar disorder and their offspring
sample_size_detail: 29 studies (13 in quantitative analysis); outcome-specific N: any anomaly N=23300 (k=11), cardiac anomalies N=1348475 (k=12), spontaneous abortion N=1289 (k=3), relapse N=48 (k=2); overall total not reported
rationale: Systematic review/meta-analysis including case-control, cohort, and interventional studies (Newcastle-Ottawa and Cochrane RoB tools used), hence Mixed.

design_detail: Prospective longitudinal PK study with serial blood sampling each trimester and postpartum; lithium elimination clearance and creatinine clearance vs nonpregnant baseline
population: Pregnant and postpartum women treated with lithium for bipolar disorder, US
sample_size_detail: 3 women completed serial sampling
rationale: Characterizes lithium clearance and concentrations across pregnancy; no confounder-adjusted clinical outcome comparison.

design_detail: Systematic review (PubMed 1995–2015) of mood stabilizer exposure through breastfeeding: relative infant dose, milk:plasma ratio, infant serum levels, adverse events
population: Breastfed infants of lactating women taking mood stabilizers
sample_size_detail: Sum of drug-specific cases: lamotrigine 122, lithium 26, carbamazepine 64, valproate 9, oxcarbazepine 2; one report covered both carbamazepine and valproate, so some overlap possible
rationale: Systematic search with included case reports, case series, and prospective/cross-sectional studies. Total N computed by summing reported drug-specific case counts (not stated as a total).

design_detail: Retrospective cohort, Kaiser Permanente Washington EHR linked to WA birth records 2001–2014; antidepressant continuers vs discontinuers among pre-pregnancy users; IPTW with GEE
severity_measure: IPTW covariates included inpatient psychiatric hospitalization, psychiatry and psychotherapy visits, and psychotropic fills (antipsychotic, benzodiazepine, mood stabilizer) in year before pregnancy, plus mental health diagnoses; PHQ-9 described but not modeled
comparison_group: Women with antidepressant fills before pregnancy who discontinued (no fill during pregnancy)
population: Singleton live births to women aged 15–45 without pre-existing diabetes, with antidepressant fill in 6 months pre-pregnancy, KPWA 2001–2014
sample_size_detail: 2845 births (1634 continuers, 1211 discontinuers) for GDM; 1101 births (613/488) for blood glucose; about 4% excluded for missing covariates
rationale: IPTW adjustment set explicitly includes 'indicators of mental health severity' such as psychiatric hospitalization and mental health care utilization. Unit is births (7% of women contributed >1 birth).
